senses.gloss:
Daidhiṣavya is mentioned in a mantra of the taittirīya Saṃhitā. Apparently the word (as derived from didhiṣū) denotes the son of a younger sister married before the elder sister, rather than the son of a woman twice married, the explanation of the St. Petersburg Dictionary.
Foot notes iii. 2, 4, 4; Kātyāyana śrauta sūtra, ii. 1, 22; kauśika sūtra, 3, 5; 137, 37.
American Journal of Philology, 17, 431, n.
